subject: Notice window & termination-for-convenience fallback matrix — BluePeak order form
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: notice windows & T4C fallback matrix — BluePeak order form

Elaine —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, attaching a short proposal for how we can handle the Term / Auto‑renew / Termination‑for‑Convenience (T4C) mechanics on the Order Form while we close the MSA redlines. High level:

- Mutual 60‑day written notice to terminate at the end of term (standard).
- For pilots / POC: no T4C during the pilot period (first 90 days).
- For commercial commit: allow T4C but with a stepped fallback matrix that preserves capacity and transition support (see summary below).

Fallback matrix (summary):
1) 0–12 months after effective date: T4C allowed, but customer pays remaining month‑of‑notice pro‑rated + one month of committed run‑rate as exit fee OR we provide 30 days of paid transition support (customer selects).
2) 12–24 months: reduced exit fee (pro‑rated remaining commitment only), 14 day notice minimum.
3) >=24 months: standard 60‑day notice, no exit fee.

We think this preserves BluePeak’s desire for flexibility while protecting Redwood on committed capacity and transition ops.

Ask: please confirm whether procurement/legal will accept the stepped matrix concept or whether you need a flat 60‑day mutual opt‑out only. If you prefer, Kimberly has a redline of the Order Form language we can share to accelerate legal review.

Attachments: BluePeak_OrderForm_T4C_redline.pdf (draft redline), MSA‑Term‑Appendix‑v3.docx (wording options).

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa —

Appreciate the summary. A few quick points from procurement/legal:

- BluePeak needs a firm 60‑day mutual notice window on the Order Form; we prefer to avoid graduated exit fees — those complicate procurement approvals.
- Pilots are negotiable but we generally require the ability to terminate during a pilot without penalty if performance objectives aren’t met.
- If you must include an exit fee for the first year, procurement will need a clear waiver path for our internal execs; that will take extra approvals.

Can Kimberly share the redline ASAP so our counsel can do a side‑by‑side? Also looping in our legal contact (legal@bluepeak.com) to confirm.

—Elaine

Hi all —

I reviewed Marissa’s proposed matrix and attached a legal redline (same file name: BluePeak_OrderForm_T4C_redline.pdf). Quick notes on legal posture:

- We can accept a flat 60‑day mutual termination provision as primary, but recommend adding an explicit carveout in the Order Form for pilots: "Pilot termination for dissatisfaction within the pilot period without penalty, provided Customer documents failure to meet mutually agreed success criteria." That addresses BluePeak’s ask while protecting Redwood.
- If Redwood insists on an exit fee for year‑one commercial commitments, the language must be time‑limited (e.g., applies only to commitments signed within first 12 months of the MSA effective date) and capped (e.g., not to exceed one month of committed fees).
- Redline includes fallbacks for data handling and transitional support obligations if T4C is exercised — we require minimal notice to flush KV caches and hand over logs; we also propose a standard 30‑day transition SLA in lieu of an exit fee for customers who need operational continuity.

Please see tracked changes in the attachment. If BluePeak legal wants to propose alternate language, we can do a redline exchange and converge offline.

Kimberly Park

Thanks Elaine — quick reply to keep things moving: we can agree to a flat 60‑day mutual notice as the default on the Order Form to match your procurement constraints. To protect capacity economics, would BluePeak consider either:

A) A one‑time, capped exit fee for commercial commitments signed within the first 12 months (not to exceed one month of committed ARR), OR
B) A guaranteed 30 days of paid transition support from Redwood (we can include a runbook deliverable) in lieu of any monetary exit fee.

Either option preserves your exec flexibility and avoids complex tiering in procurement approvals. If BluePeak prefers, we can put Option B into the Order Form and leave Option A as an amendment that requires executive signoff.

Next steps: Kimberly’s redline is attached for your review. If this approach looks acceptable, Kimberly and BluePeak legal can exchange tracked changes and we’ll publish a clean Order Form for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa
